newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The won finished lower against the dollar on Wednesday as banks bought dollars to cover their positions, traders said.
The won closed at 829.10, compared with the day's opening rate of 828.30. It moved in a range of 828.20 to 829.50.
Traders said many banks accumulated the U.S. currency as the market was seen short of dollars. The won was also weak because importer deals outpaced export negotiations.
But the downside was limited in the afternoon on expected month-end export negotiations in coming days.
"Today's (dollar) rise could be seen as a technical rebound following the recent fall," said a dealer from an American bank.
Dealers said the won was seen fluctuating in a range of 828.00 to 829.50 on Thursday. The central bank set the base mid-rate for Thursday at 828.90 versus 828.00 for Wednesday.
